plan.angle: The top results for customer information form are blank templates and printable sheets that collect a name, phone and address once and stop there. Nothing shows what happens to the record afterward: the same customer filled in twice, a wholesale account typed into the accounting system by hand, an address that went stale two years ago, a property manager with four sites crammed into one address line. This page is for the small business that keeps one record per customer: a form that matches returning customers by phone number, sends new wholesale accounts to the accounting system, asks plan customers to confirm their details once a year, and holds several service sites under one account. Intake questionnaires, credit applications and contact forms stay on their own pages.
tab_stories: Pellstone Auto Repair checks customers in on a counter tablet that asks for the phone number first; on a Saturday with 18 check-ins, 11 phone numbers matched an existing record and updated it, 7 started new records, and service writer Nikolai Brisbin sees each one tagged Returning or New.

Dunmere Coffee Roasters opens wholesale accounts for cafes; Saltgrass Cafe enters its billing address, a separate ship-to address, an accounts payable email and delivery hours of 7 to 10 a.m., the app creates the customer in QuickBooks, and account manager Kalani Vukovic gets an email that a new account is in.

Gorsefield Heating and Air emails its 340 maintenance plan customers a link each January to confirm their phone, address and equipment; 212 confirmed with no changes, 31 changed something and land on office manager Mariela Petrosyan's review list, and 97 have not answered yet.

Thistlebrook Pest Control services Harbor Row Properties, one customer with one billing contact and 4 service sites; each site has its own gate code and access notes, and the technician opens the site record on the route instead of calling the office.
